When calling this API to create a media file, you need to upload the corresponding media file to the OBS bucket of VOD. If the media file to be uploaded is smaller than 20 MB, use the PUT method to upload the file to the URL returned by the API. For details, see [Example 1: Uploading a Media File Less Than 20 MB](https://support.huaweicloud.com/en-us/api-vod/vod_04_0195.html). If the media file to be uploaded is larger than 20 MB, it must be split into binary streams before being uploaded. For details about how to use this API, see [Example 2: Uploading a Media File More Than 20 MB by Part](https://support.huaweicloud.com/en-us/api-vod/vod_04_0216.html).

This API is an asynchronous API. After an audio extraction task is created and delivered, asset_id and the extracted audio_asset_id are returned. However, the audio extraction task is not complete immediately. You can check whether the audio extraction task is complete in the audio extraction completion event on the event notification page.

After media files are published, you can call this API to request CDN for media file pre-loading by ID or URL. Upon the first request, the CDN caches the requested media file for faster download and better user experience. One tenant can pre-load a maximum of 1,000 media files per day.

Synchronizes audio/video files stored in OBS buckets to VOD through inventory hosting OBS hosting can be incremental or inventory hosting. Incremental hosting can be configured only on the VOD console. After it is configured, new audio/video files added to OBS will be automatically synchronized to VOD. For details, see [Incremental Hosting](https://support.huaweicloud.com/en-us/usermanual-vod/vod010032.html). You need to authorize VOD to access the target OBS bucket for incremental or inventory hosting. For details, see [Bucket Authorization](https://support.huaweicloud.com/en-us/usermanual-vod/vod010031.html).

If you have stored audio/video files in an OBS bucket before using VOD, you can call this API to dump the files to VOD so that VOD can manage your files. Before calling this API, you need to call the API for [Authorizing Access to OBS](https://support.huaweicloud.com/en-us/api-vod/vod_04_0199.html) to authorize VOD to access the OBS bucket where the audio/video files are stored.
Sets the status of the media file to published. Media files can be published in batches.

The CDN cache of media assets in the completed, deleted, or published status can be updated by the specified asset ID or URL to force the cached resources on CDN PoPs to expire. When a user accesses CDN the next time, the latest resource is pulled from the origin server, returned to the user, and cached on CDN PoPs. One tenant can update a maximum of 1,000 media assets per day.

When a device plays an encrypted HLS video, the device requests a key from the tenant management system, which checks whether there are keys cached locally. If not, this API is called to query the key from VOD. For details about where this API is applied, see [Protecting Videos with HLS Encryption](https://support.huaweicloud.com/en-us/bestpractice-vod/vod_10_0004.html).

When a client requests for creating a media file greater than 20 MB, the media file needs to be uploaded to OBS by part. The client needs to obtain the authorization using this API each time before uploading a file part to OBS. Obtains temporarily authorized URLs of APIs for [Initializing a Multipart Task](https://support.huaweicloud.com/en-us/api-obs/obs_04_0098.html), [Multipart Upload](https://support.huaweicloud.com/en-us/api-obs/obs_04_0099.html), [Merging Parts into a Complete Object](https://support.huaweicloud.com/en-us/api-obs/obs_04_0102.html), [Listing Uploaded Parts of an Object](https://support.huaweicloud.com/en-us/api-obs/obs_04_0101.html), and [Canceling a Multipart Upload Task](https://support.huaweicloud.com/en-us/api-obs/obs_04_0103.html). You need to configure the HTTP request method, header, and body according to the OBS API reference, and then request for the desired temporarily authorized URL. The multipart upload method is the same as that in the OBS API reference, including the HTTP request method, request header, and request body. This API is used to generate a URL with authentication information (query_str) to replace the URL in the OBS API, so that the user has the temporary permission for uploading files to the bucket of VOD. When calling the API for obtaining authorization, input bucket, object_key, and http_verb. bucket and object_key are obtained from the target field in the response body returned by the API for [Uploading Media Files to VOD](https://support.huaweicloud.com/en-us/api-vod/vod_04_0196.html). http_verb varies depending on the specified operation. This API is of v1.1 and does not support front-end cross-origin access, but supports back-end access. If front-end cross-origin access is required, use the API of v1.0. For details, see [Obtaining Authorization for Multipart Upload](vod_04_0009.xml). The response by the API of v1.1 does not require combining the URL. Obtain **sign_str** in the response and then send the request.

After a media file is created, upload a thumbnail, update a video file, or update the existing thumbnail. After a video file is updated, call the API for [Confirming Media Upload](https://support.huaweicloud.com/en-us/api-vod/vod_04_0198.html) to notify VOD. You do not need to call the API after updating or uploading a thumbnail. You can upload an updated video by part. For details, see [Example 2: Uploading a Media File More Than 20 MB by Part](https://support.huaweicloud.com/en-us/api-vod/vod_04_0216.html).

Changes the OBS storage class of a media asset. By default, the **Standard** storage class applies to media asset upload. You can change the storage class to **Infrequent Access** or **Archive**. - **Infrequent Access** can be restored to **Standard** or downgraded to **Archive**. - **Archive** can only be restored to **Standard** and cannot be directly changed to **Infrequent Access**. The minimum storage period of **Infrequent Access** is 30 days, and that of **Archive** is 90 days. If media assets are retrieved or deleted before the storage period expires, you will still be charged based on the minimum storage period. You will be charged for media asset retrieval when restoring the storage class from **Infrequent Access** or **Archive** to **Standard**.
